q: Do electricity imports from Bhutan and Nepal change India's grid emission factor?
title: Electricity imports and India's grid factor
short: Only a little. CEA counts imports at zero emissions. In FY 2025-26 the weighted average was 0.678 t CO2 per MWh excluding cross-border transfers and 0.675 including them, with net imports of 7,622 GWh. Use the adjusted figure, 0.675, which is the one CEA headlines.
audience: Sustainability teams reconciling slightly different CEA figures in reports

p: The CDM grid tool lets the database show both. India trades power with Bhutan, Nepal, Bangladesh and Myanmar, and CEA applies an emission factor of zero to imports from other countries.
Use the adjusted 0.675 for Scope 2. If a buyer quotes 0.678 they are reading the unadjusted row; the difference is under half a percent.

senseible: Senseible reads electricity bills into dated kWh records per meter and site, so whichever CEA factor and version you apply, each Scope 2 figure traces back to the bill and the factor behind it.
